Definition: to be alert, physically (on foot) or mentally (in courage)
BiblicalUsage: To be alert, to be strong and of good courage, and the Bible says it to men who are afraid. Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them, Moses tells Israel at the Jordan. Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage, God tells Joshua at the same river; and David tells Solomon, Be strong and of good courage, and do it: fear not, nor be dismayed: for the LORD God, even my God, will be with thee.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe courage in the Bible is not a temper but a command, given three times at three rivers of fear, and always with the same reason: God goes with you. Moses says it to a people about to fight, God says it to a man about to lead, and David says it to a son about to build. I hold that the courage is not in me but in the company — He will not fail thee, nor forsake thee, and that is the whole of it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
